Kansas splits by animal type: trained service animals have a strong independent basis (K.S.A. 39-1102/1107/1108, statutory no-fee rule, criminal backing at 39-1103); ESAs are expressly excluded from that statute by 39-1113(f), leaving only the generic KAAD duty at 44-1016(h)(3)(B) (textually independent of federal law but judicially untested in housing -- no KS case extends employment-side FHA lockstep to housing). Real conflict found in the generic clause: its flat "10 days to cure" for landlord-initiated termination doesn't match Kansas's actual 14-day cure period (§58-2564(a)); a lease clause contractually shortening a statutory cure period is arguably itself a waiver of Act rights prohibited under §58-2547(a)(1), not just a wrong number. Wallace, 233 Kan.). §58-2572(b) routes the retaliation remedy through this same section.

MATERIAL CORRECTION 2026-08-29: an earlier draft incorrectly described this as parallel to Wyoming's §35-13-203(b) service-animal-fraud finding. The parallel is false: Wyoming's penalty is scoped to rights 'set forth in this article' (which includes housing), while Kansas's §39-1112 is scoped by a place list that excludes housing -- so unlike Wyoming, this penalty does NOT reach residential leasing. Valid citation, false characterization -- a citation-existence check alone could not have caught this. Proof of absence by repeated legislative refusal: HB 2523 (2019), SB 360 and S Sub HB 2057 (2022), SB 170 (2025) all failed to enact a Kansas ESA-fraud housing penalty.
